Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Technologies Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud Technologies' results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Product Officer; Casey Wong, Chief Marketing Officer; Riley Chen, Chief Sales Officer; and Alex Harper, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud continued its strong growth trajectory in Q2, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included expanding our presence in emerging markets, accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform, enhancing our developer ecosystem, strengthening our commitment to sustainability, investing in employee training and development, improving cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

I'm thrilled to dive into our cloud services revenue performance, which remains the cornerstone of AetherCloud's growth story. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, cloud services revenue reached a record $26.4 billion, representing 17% year-over-year growth and 8% quarter-over-quarter growth. This marks our 15th consecutive quarter of at least 15% year-over-year expansion in this segment, underscoring the secular tailwinds in cloud adoption amid accelerating AI workloads, enterprise digital transformation, and edge computing proliferation.

Our trailing twelve-month cloud services revenue now stands at $102.8 billion, with net revenue retention holding steady at 118%, reflecting strong existing customer expansion. Our cloud services portfolio—spanning Infrastructure-as-a-Service, Platform-as-a-Service, and Software-as-a-Service—saw balanced contributions. IaaS revenue came in at $14.2 billion, up 20% year-over-year and 10% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by surging compute and storage demand, particularly from AI training clusters. Our EC2-equivalent instances grew 25% year-over-year, with GPU utilization spiking 45% due to AetherGPU clusters powered by NVIDIA H100s and upcoming Blackwell architectures. Storage volumes, led by our S3-like AetherObject service, expanded 22% year-over-year to over 15 exabytes under management, benefiting from data lakehouse integrations with partners like Snowflake and Databricks.

PaaS revenue was $8.1 billion, up 15% year-over-year and 6% quarter-over-quarter. Key here was our Kubernetes-orchestrated AetherContainer service, which saw 30% year-over-year adoption growth among Fortune 500 enterprises. Serverless offerings, including AetherFunctions—our Lambda analog—contributed 18% of PaaS revenue, up from 14% a year ago, as developers shift to event-driven architectures for cost efficiency. SaaS revenue hit $4.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. Our AetherAI platform, integrating foundation models akin to Azure OpenAI Service, drove 35% year-over-year growth within SaaS, with over 2,500 customers deploying custom LLMs. Database-as-a-Service like AetherAurora rounded out the segment, with multi-tenant efficiencies yielding 90% gross margins.

Excluding foreign exchange impacts, year-over-year growth would have been 18%, highlighting the underlying strength despite a modest USD headwind. AI and generative AI workload explosion now accounts for 28% of total cloud services, up from 18% year-over-year, mirroring trends at peers like AWS and Google Cloud. We onboarded 450 new AI/ML customers, including a $500 million multi-year deal with a leading hyperscaler for sovereign AI inference. Our AetherBedrock model marketplace, with 150+ third-party models, saw inference API calls surge 60% quarter-over-quarter, driving attach rates of 40% on new IaaS commitments.

Enterprise cloud migrations and workload modernization also played a big role—we facilitated migrations for 120 large enterprises, shifting 15% more mainframe workloads to cloud via our AetherMainframe service, which offers z/OS emulation at one-third the cost. Hybrid cloud solutions, compatible with VMware Tanzu and Red Hat OpenShift, reduced customer TCO by 35%, boosting multi-year contracts worth $3.2 billion in new ARR. Edge and 5G/6G synergies drove edge computing revenue up 40% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, powered by AetherEdge nodes deployed in 5,000+ telco sites globally. Partnerships with Ericsson and Nokia for private 5G networks positioned us ahead of the IoT data deluge, with latency-sensitive workloads like autonomous vehicles contributing early wins.

Pricing discipline and efficiencies added momentum, with strategic price adjustments on mature services like 5-10% hikes on legacy block storage contributing 2 points to year-over-year growth, while commitment-based discounts via Savings Plans captured 65% of new capacity. Customer unit economics improved, with average revenue per enterprise account up 12% year-over-year to $45 million. Our developer ecosystem momentum, through free tier expansions and GitHub Copilot-like AetherDevAssist tool, attracted 1.2 million new developers, converting 22% to paid usage within 90 days—faster than industry benchmarks.

Growth was geographically diversified: Americas at 52% of revenue with $13.7 billion, up 16% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter, featuring U.S. public sector deals including a $1.2 billion DoD contract for cloud sovereignty; EMEA at 28% with $7.4 billion, up 19% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter, driven by sovereign cloud regions in Germany and France compliant with Schrems II and NIS2; APAC at 20% with $5.3 billion, up 17% year-over-year and 10% quarter-over-quarter, exploding in India with UPI 2.0 integrations and strong Japan uptake. Emerging markets now represent 15% of cloud revenue, up from 10% year-over-year.

Strategically, we're doubling down on sustainable hyperscale infrastructure, commissioning 12 new data centers this quarter for total capacity up 25% year-over-year to 45 gigawatts, with 40% powered by renewables. Our Project GreenCloud initiative cut PUE to 1.15, improving margins. Looking ahead, we see Q3 cloud services revenue growing 16-18% year-over-year, with AI comprising 32% of mix.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 25% year-over-year to $28 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 72%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 32%.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now dive into our key achievements from Q2 and outline the strategic priorities that will propel AetherCloud into the next phase of hypergrowth in the cloud computing landscape. The cloud industry is navigating a perfect storm of AI-driven demand, macroeconomic headwinds, and geopolitical fragmentation, with IDC projecting global cloud infrastructure spending to hit $1.1 trillion by 2027, growing at a 20% CAGR. We've positioned ourselves at the forefront, delivering outsized results while executing on our multi-year roadmap.

Total revenue reached $28 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter—well ahead of our guide and consensus. This was driven by a 35% year-over-year surge in our core IaaS and PaaS segments, now 72% of total revenue, reflecting robust demand for our hyperscale data centers and AI-optimized compute. Annual Recurring Revenue hit a record $105 billion, growing 28% year-over-year, with Remaining Performance Obligations at $47.2 billion, up 41% year-over-year. Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate expanded to 128%, meaning existing customers expanded spend by 28% on average while adopting new workloads at an accelerating pace. We added 1,200 new customers exceeding $1 million in ARR, including a Fortune 10 financial services giant migrating 60% of its on-prem VMware workloads to our hybrid cloud and a leading European automaker deploying our AutoML services for Level 4 autonomous driving simulations.

On the AI front, our AetherAI suite—powered by proprietary tensor processing units and NVIDIA H100 GPUs—saw explosive adoption. AI and machine learning services revenue grew 62% year-over-year to $7.4 billion, accounting for 35% of total revenue. We processed over 15 exaflops of AI training workloads, a 75% increase from Q1, fueled by generative AI use cases, including our partnership with OpenAI for fine-tuned models on sovereign cloud regions compliant with GDPR and the EU AI Act.

Regionally, North America at 55% of revenue grew 29% year-over-year; EMEA delivered 45% growth to $7.8 billion with new renewable-powered regions in Frankfurt and Paris; APAC-Pacific exploded 52% to $5.6 billion, with Japan and India shining through sovereign AI workloads; even LatAm grew 22% via edge expansions. Operationally, GAAP operating income was $5.6 billion, adjusted operating margins expanded 400 basis points to 32.5%. CapEx was $3.2 billion, focused on AI data center builds adding 1.2 gigawatts. Free cash flow was $2.1 billion, with $15.4 billion in cash.

Per Synergy Research, we gained 2.2 points of public cloud market share to 24% globally, closing the gap on leaders while outpacing in enterprise AI via multi-cloud interoperability.

Moving forward, our priorities focus on AI ubiquity, global sovereignty, and sustainable hyperscale, backed by $12 billion in FY24 investments toward $50 billion ARR by 2027. For AI ubiquity, Q3 brings AetherAI 2.0 with serverless inference at 10x lower latency, integrated vector database for RAG, 100 petaflops of new GPU capacity including NVIDIA Blackwell, and QuantumAgents for autonomous workflows, targeting 50% revenue from AI/ML by FY25 via Anthropic and xAI partnerships.

For global sovereignty and edge, $4 billion for 15 new regions by 2026 like Riyadh-1 and Jakarta-2 with quantum-resistant encryption; QuantumEdge spans 5,000 nodes for 5G slicing, capturing 30% edge market by 2028. For sustainable hyperscale, Scope 1 and 2 emissions down 48% year-over-year with PUE at 1.08, piloting fusion-powered data centers for carbon-negative by 2030. M&A opportunistic post-Nebula Data acquisition.

Q2 validates execution; we reaffirm FY24 revenue guide of $34.5-35.0 billion and raise adjusted EBITDA to $14.8 billion.

Next, I'd like to introduce Taylor Kim, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI-powered confidential computing.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now turn to our outlook on macroeconomic factors and their expected impact on AetherCloud's business through FY24 and into FY25. The cloud computing industry has proven resilient amid global headwinds, driven by unrelenting demand for AI, machine learning workloads, and digital transformation. However, we're mindful of elevated interest rates, persistent inflation, geopolitical tensions, and uneven recoveries.

Globally, we assume modestly slowing GDP growth around 2.8% for 2024 per IMF, with Fed terminal rate at 4.5-5.0%, tempering enterprise capex. Net new ARR additions were $1.2 billion, 18% year-over-year but below target due to sales cycles at 120 days. We expect FY24 total revenue growth of 22-25% to $48-50 billion, lower end reflecting migration delays.

Inflation drags costs, with energy up 20-25% year-over-year pressuring non-GAAP operating margins to 32-34%, down 150 basis points despite 92% GPU utilization. Mitigating via GreenScale targeting 60% renewables by year-end, shaving 5-7% off power costs by FY25.

Regionally: North America, 62% of revenue, 28-30% growth on hybrid adoption and AI, though SMB pullback prompts Pay-As-You-Scale pricing for 98% NRR. EMEA, 22%, 15-18% tempered by energy crisis, but boosted by EU-localized storage; hedging 80% FX. APAC, 12%, 25-28% on Japan mandates and India infrastructure, with $1.8 billion capex. Rest of World 20% volatile but offset by wins like Petrobras.

Counter-cyclically, generative AI $200 billion TAM by 2025 drives commitments up 60% quarter-over-quarter via Nimbus AI Fabric for Fortune 500 in autonomous driving and drug discovery. Edge via Nokia 5G MEC targets $10 billion market.

While macro adds 3-5 points conservatism, $28 billion RPO and 115% net expansion provide visibility; headwinds peak mid-FY24.

Now, I'll pass it to Morgan Patel for a product update.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. We recently launched AetherAI 2.0, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our Average Revenue Per User—or ARPU—metrics, a cornerstone of our financial health and indicator of customer expansion in cloud. We define ARPU as total annualized recurring revenue from IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS divided by active accounts, excluding one-time services.

Full-year blended ARPU reached $142,000, up 22% year-over-year from $116,000. Q2 ARPU hit $148,500, up 7% sequentially and 28% year-over-year, underscoring value realization. Enterprise ARPU over $1 million ACV surged to $2.84 million, 31% year-over-year, from multi-year AI commitments and Kubernetes migrations like Nexara Kubernetes Service, where a Fortune 50 retailer scaled to 5,000 nodes with GenAI endpoints. Mid-market ARPU grew 19% to $285,000 via self-serve and FinOps.

NRR at 128% full-year, expansion cohorts 145%, reflecting land-and-expand into serverless and DBaaS at 40% attach rates.

Regionally: Americas 52% revenue, ARPU up 25% to $162,000 on hyperscaler displacement with 15-20% lower TCO; EMEA up 18% to $131,000 on GDPR edge; APAC fastest at 29% to $118,000 from GenAI pilots like Japanese automaker's VectorDB.

Drivers: AI monetization via Nexara AI Studio 45% uplift; observability with Guardrails 92% retention; FinOps dynamic pricing 15% expansion.

Guide 20-24% ARPU growth 2024, backed by $18.7 billion RPO up 36%. ARPU proves platform depth for AI era.

I'll now hand it over to Casey Wong to discuss our marketing strategy.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Morgan. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our financials, I'd like to highlight Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, our key forward-looking metric representing executed contracts not yet recognized—focusing on committed subscriptions excluding usage-based.

Total RPO at quarter-end $47.2 billion, up 29% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, 11th straight acceleration outpacing 24% revenue growth. Current RPO $19.8 billion up 34% year-over-year and 10% quarter-over-quarter, 82% in next six months. Non-current $27.4 billion up 26%, average contract 28 months on GPU AI commitments.

NRR 118%, up from 114%, 125% expansion especially AI upsells over 140%.

Geographically: Americas $25.1 billion up 25% on Fortune 500 AI; EMEA $12.4 billion up 35% sovereign GDPR SAP migrations; APAC $9.7 billion up 42% Arm instances and telco edge, now 21% total.

45% RPO increase from AI contracts via CloudForge AI Fabric NVIDIA integrations; hybrid ForgeBridge; 25% new RPO carbon-neutral.

In $679 billion 2024 market per Gartner, our 29% growth beats peers; FY25 27-30% total RPO. $47.2 billion de-risks $12 billion FY24 revenue.

Next, I'd like to introduce Riley Chen, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Casey. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in Q2, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before details, forward-looking statements subject to risks per SEC. Our FY24 revenue guide 27% growth to $38-40 billion, accelerating FY25, on 85% recurring ARR to $32 billion, RPO $105 billion up 45%.

Revenue assumptions: 60% incremental from workload/AI growth, 50% GPU compute via Aether AI Fabric, ARPU to $2.5 million at 75% utilization; risk if partnerships consolidate. Customer acquisition 1,200 net logos, enterprise 25% expansion, churn <4%; SMB 35% via Edge. Regional: NA 42% 25% sovereign FedRAMP; EMEA 28% 32% telco; APAC 25% 38%; LATAM 5% 20%. Product: IaaS/PaaS 65% 28%, SaaS 20% 35%, services 15%. IDC $1.1T 2027 tailwinds.

Profitability: margins 32% FY24 up 300bps, EBITDA 38%, FCF $12-14B. Gross 72.5% on 87% utilization PUE efficiency, renewables; OpEx 22% with AI efficiencies; CapEx 12-14% AI/network/edge.

Positioning AI-native multi-cloud with Kubernetes NVIDIA partnerships; sustainability ESG. Conservative assumptions grounded in RPO/NRR.

Finally, I'll pass it to Alex Harper to discuss our security initiatives.

Alex Harper:
Thank you, Riley. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we discuss performance, key is investments in security infrastructure and personnel. In cloud where hyperscalers hold 65% share per Synergy, security builds trust amid 150% ransomware surge per Sophos and SolarWinds risks. We allocated $1.2 billion FY24 to date, up 28% year-over-year, 14% R&D 8% revenue, ahead of Gartner 10-12% average.

Infrastructure $785 million: $420 million data centers with confidential computing on 85% instances like Nitro Enclaves; $150 million zero-trust with Palo Alto CrowdStrike, 92% risk reduction per Mandiant; $120 million Sentinel AI detecting 1.7 million DDoS via Cloudflare; $95 million post-quantum Kyber/Dilithium, 30% migrated; FedRAMP High unlocked $250 million public sector. APAC 35%, EMEA 28% GDPR, NA 25% multi-cloud.

Personnel $415 million: team to 2,800 FTEs up 32%, $285K comp; $50 million Security Academy with SANS trained 1,200, cut contractors 40%; security champions in squads slashed vulnerabilities 65%. APAC 40% hires, EMEA 30% NIS2.

ROI: spend dipped to 8%, NPS to 78 driving 22% upsell, churn <0.5%. FY24 $1.5-1.6 billion ramp for edge AI red-teaming. Differentiates in hybrid, 68% enterprises per Flexera.

Back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Ross:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. Can you elaborate on the AI contribution to growth and your capex plans for GPU capacity?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. AI is now 28% of cloud services and driving 35% of total revenue growth, with 450 new customers and key deals like the $500 million hyperscaler sovereign AI. We're processing 15 exaflops, up 75% quarter-over-quarter. Capex at $3.2 billion this quarter focuses 70% on AI data centers, adding 1.2 gigawatts including H100/H200 and Blackwell ramps, with 500 megawatt NVIDIA commitments mitigating supply risks. This supports Q3 16-18% cloud growth with AI at 32%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. On macro headwinds, how are you factoring them into FY24 guidance, especially regional variances and margins?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. We've built 3-5 points conservatism into 22-25% FY24 revenue growth to $48-50 billion, with elongated cycles and inflation on energy up 20-25%. North America strong at 28-30%, EMEA tempered 15-18% hedged FX, APAC bright 25-28%. Margins 32-34% via GreenScale renewables and 92% utilization; RPO $47.2 billion and 115% NRR provide buffer, reacceleration H2 on rate cuts and AI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. Taylor, on the tech roadmap, how are security integrations evolving with AI workloads?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, David. Security is embedded, with $1.2 billion investments including confidential computing on 85% instances and post-quantum pilots. For AI, Sentinel AI processes petabytes for threat detection, zero-trust with CrowdStrike, and ForgeBridge for hybrid security. This drove NPS to 78 and <0.5% churn on high-security, positioning for AI red-teaming in FY24.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
